newsitem.title: LATVIA: FORECAST-Latvian PM sees 10 percent 1997 inflation.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Latvian PM sees 10 percent 1997 inflation.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele forecast on Friday that the country would experience inflation of 10 percent in 1997 and said he was determined to push through a balanced budget for next year.
"Planned inflation will be 10 percent if we carry on being as purposeful and as politically determined as we have been," Shkele told a news conference.
The forecast is slightly below previous estimates by government officials of a 12 percent rise in prices. Inflation in 1996 is expected at 16 to 18 percent.
Shkele came to power with the aim of getting the economy back in order after a severe banking crisis last year.
"1997 will be a decisive year for Latvia, showing whether we are capable of starting a new life or not," Shkele said.
Shkele has set a 1996 budget with a 40 million lat deficit and has staked his political career on attaining a balanced budget next year.
Shkele said he was opposed to any major changes in the budget and reiterated it must be passed without a deficit.
"I will not continue to work if we have a budget deficit," Shkele said.
